photos.c: Belgrave's 'winning team' of Hall, Piddington and Bonsor are pictured above--what prospects!.

FRONTISPIECE (Photo: Ed Lacey)--Who's that guy with George Piddington? Well, George condescendingly turned away his own autograph hunters to allow some Aussie fella called Ron Clarke to join him in a grin at Ed Lacey. They were front and back markers in a 1500 metres handicap at White City. We leave you to guess which was which!

The Belgrave 20 Mile Road Race. Centre: Graham Taylor (Camb H), the winner. Top left to right: Geoff Pearson, George Piddington, Alan Black and Trevor Hart. Bottom: John Davies, Bob Richardson and Charlie Henn.

George Piddington pictured during the Belgrave '20'. At this stage his antennae must have been malfunctioning for he does not seem to have detected 'the grey ghost', Hon. Treasurer John Baker, creeping up behind.

Opposite page. The Philips 100x1 mile relay. Top right: Charlie Gillett. Centre left to right: Dudley Gordon, Gerry Sexton, George Piddington and Robin Brown. Bottom left to right: Simon Pritchard, Joe McDonald and Alan Painter.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.

Above:  At the White City Stadium, in 1968,  the Fire Brigade Sports 1500 metres handicap brought together the then world record holder Ron Clarke of Australia … and George Piddington of Belgrave Harriers. We’ll leave you to decided which one was the front marker and which one was off “scratch”.

Part of the Belgrave coaching course 1965
Amongst those standing are Ben Lulham (far left), George Piddington (4th from left), Frank Simmons (6th from left) Jack Hampshire Snr and Charlie Jones (both partly hidden) and Tom Carter (far right).
